hh.name: HeadHunter (hh.ru)
hh.metaTitle: Track hh.ru applications automatically and for free
hh.metaDescription: How to track applications on hh.ru, hh.kz and rabota.by: the heyreply extension records an application when you send it and updates statuses from the My applications page.
hh.intro: On hh.ru applications get lost quickly: dozens of vacancies, invitations that arrive a week later, and a list that never shows the big picture. The heyreply extension logs every application in a table and pulls statuses from the same pages, without your hh.ru password.
captured: Vacancy and company name, link to the vacancy
City, work format and salary range when the vacancy states them
Application date: when you send it and when you open My applications
Source: HeadHunter is filled in automatically
hh.status: Every few hours while you are on hh.ru, the extension reads My applications (hh.ru/applicant/negotiations) in the background and updates statuses in heyreply, such as an invitation or a rejection — no need to open it. This also picks up applications made in the hh mobile app. Older applications are added with their real dates when the board shows them. It works on hh.ru, hh.kz and rabota.by.
steps: Install the heyreply extension for Chrome or Firefox.
In heyreply open Settings → Integrations, create a token and paste it into the extension together with the site address.
Apply on hh.ru as usual. Open My applications from time to time to pull in statuses.
tips: "Viewed" on hh.ru is not yet a reply from the employer: heyreply keeps it as a separate status, so you can see how many applications were even opened.
Compare sources in the statistics to see which board gives more interviews for the same number of applications.

guideConversion.metaTitle: Job application conversion rate: how to calculate and improve it
guideConversion.metaDescription: What the conversion of an application into an interview and an offer means, how to calculate it, why the average number tells you little, and what you can learn by comparing job boards and resumes.
guideConversion.h1: Job application conversion: how to calculate it and what to do with it
guideConversion.lead: Once you have dozens of applications, "why aren't they calling?" turns into guesswork. Conversion answers it with numbers: what share of applications reaches a reply, an interview and an offer, and where the funnel narrows the most. Below: how to calculate it, how to read the result, and the mistakes that make it useless.

p: Conversion is the share of applications that reach the next stage. A job search is easy to picture as a funnel: application, employer's reply, recruiter call, test task, interview, offer. At every stage some candidates drop out, and each transition has its own cause.

That is why a single number, "how many applications led to an offer", explains little. It is more useful to look at several transitions separately: then you see what exactly is not working instead of just feeling unlucky.
On the overview page heyreply calculates these figures, each as a share of all applications in the selected period:
list: Reply rate: applications that got any reply (a view is not a reply; an invitation or a rejection is) divided by all applications.
Interview conversion: applications that reached an interview divided by all applications.
Offer conversion: applications that ended in an offer divided by all applications.
Ghosting: applications that never got a reply within a set time (two weeks by default, adjustable) divided by all applications.
Median time to reply: the typical number of days between applying and the first reply. The median beats the average because one reply after two months does not distort it.
p2: The funnel also shows the step between neighbouring stages, for example what share of those who passed screening got a test task. It helps you find the narrowest point.

p: Suppose over 90 days you sent 100 applications (the numbers are illustrative). 40 got a reply: the reply rate is 40%. 12 reached an interview: interview conversion is 12%. 3 turned into offers: offer conversion is 3%. 45 got no reply: ghosting is 45%.

These numbers show that your resume and applications do not work so badly (40% reply), and the main loss happens between a reply and an interview: only 12 of 40 replies became invitations. So look at how you handle screening and whether the jobs fit your experience, instead of sending another hundred applications.
The overall conversion mixes everything: top jobs and random ones, cold applications and referrals, different resumes. Comparisons inside one search are what inform:
list: By job board: on LinkedIn, Indeed and Habr Career reply rates usually differ noticeably, and you need your own values, not someone else's.
By position and level: applications for a role above your level convert differently from those for a familiar one.
By resume version and cover letter: tag which resume you sent and compare after a couple of weeks.
By how you applied: directly, through a recruiter or by referral. A referral almost always converts better, which is a good reason to spend time on networking.
p2: For this heyreply stores a source, position, work format and tags on every application, and the analytics pages calculate the same metrics separately for each source, position and location.

sections.h: Common mistakes when reading the numbers
list: A small sample. If a board has only 8 applications, one offer gives "12%", which proves nothing. Compare segments once each has at least a few dozen applications, and treat a difference of a couple of percent as noise.

Immature applications. Applications from the last few days are still waiting for a reply, so their conversion is understated. Use a period that ended at least two or three weeks ago, or look at the median time to reply.
Mixing different goals. If you apply to different roles at once, the overall figure describes your mix, not you. Split segments by position.

Auto-replies. A template rejection an hour after you applied is a reply too, but not an assessment of you as a candidate. It usually points to a filter on formal criteria (experience, salary, city) rather than the quality of your resume.

Counting from memory. Forgotten and unrecorded applications make the picture look better than it is: you remember the successful ones. Record applications at the moment you send them, preferably automatically.

p: Move through the funnel from left to right and fix the narrowest transition:
list: Few replies: check your resume and headline, the list of jobs (do the requirements fit), and when you apply. Applying within the first day of a posting often helps.
Replies but no invitations: clarify salary and format expectations, and reread the posting before the screening call.
Invitations but no offers: practise interviews and collect feedback after rejections. In heyreply you can record the reason for a rejection, and over time you see whether it repeats.
A lot of ghosting: shorten your waiting time and move to channels that reply more often, such as referrals and direct contacts.

sections.h: How to avoid counting by hand
p: A manual spreadsheet works while there are few applications. Later it gets hard to keep updated, and the data goes stale. heyreply adds applications automatically through a browser extension (hh.ru, LinkedIn, Habr Career, Indeed and 22 more boards), pulls statuses from the My applications pages and calculates the figures above itself, with filters by period, source and position. It is free and needs no job board passwords.

faq.a: Nothing. The service is free: no subscriptions, no ads and no feature limits. If it is useful, you can support the author with a voluntary donation.

faq.q: Do I need my hh.ru or LinkedIn password?
faq.a: No. The extension runs in your browser under your own session and sends heyreply only the vacancy details and the application status.
26: Russian and international job sites and the applicant tracking systems companies use (Greenhouse, Lever, Workable, Ashby). The full list is above.

faq.q: How do I connect the extension?
faq.a: Install the extension for Chrome or Firefox, create a token in Settings → Integrations and paste it into the extension together with the address of the service.

faq.q: What if my job board is not on the list?
faq.a: Add the application by hand: company, position and status take about ten seconds. Statistics are calculated exactly as for imported applications.

faq.q: Where is my data stored, and can I take it with me?
faq.a: Your data is kept on the heyreply server and is visible only to you. You can export it to CSV or JSON and delete the account entirely. See the privacy policy for details.

landing.bottomText: Signing up takes a minute and costs nothing.
